label: GO step after a rewarded trial, when the agent strongly commits to a1 (before late episode)
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1 or D2), and only when the previous trial was rewarded (99.9% of mass) and the agent is about to pick a1 with a strongly confident policy (choice logit > 8 holds 99.6% of mass; it essentially never fires before an a2 choice). It is therefore an a1-specific win-stay-commit signal, mostly when S1 is the good state. Activity drops off late in the episode and is about zero after trial ~80, so an ep_trial < 75 cutoff removes many false positives. Magnitude is largest on the first rewarded a1 trial after an unrewarded one and decays over a run of consecutive rewarded a1 trials. Those long reward streaks make up most of the remaining false positives, but a streak-length predicate scored worse than the time cutoff. Every variable used is observed: prev_reward is the D1 input, and choice is the agent own policy output at that step. Dev: P 0.74, R 0.95, F1 0.84.

issues: Phase claim holds: GO carries 100% of activation mass, D1 and D2 have 0 active steps.

prev_reward claim holds: prev_reward==1 carries 0.999 of the mass. One unstated point: the feature needs the previous trial to have been COMMON-rewarded (prev_common==0 carries 0.001 of the mass), so it is really 'S1 just paid off'. Restricting to prev_state==2 gives 0 predicted steps, so choice>8 already filters out rare-rewarded cases implicitly. Adding prev_common!=0 changes test F1 only from 0.833 to 0.837.
a1 claim holds: action==2 has 4 of 51246 active steps, and choice >= 8.07 carries 0.996 of the mass.

Fade and streak claims hold, and they are the main systematic false-positive class. Precision of the base predicate by episode time (dev): 0.95 for trials 0-24, 0.85 for 25-49, 0.49 for 50-74, 0.05 for 75+. By streak (test): 0.90 when trial t-2 was unrewarded vs 0.59 when the two previous trials were also rewarded. This is a graded decay, so the hard ep_trial<75 cutoff is a coarse proxy. The explanation openly acknowledges these false positives, so I do not count them as a refutation.
Cutoff choice is slightly off: ep_trial<65 scores better than <75 (dev F1 0.854 vs 0.84; test P 0.814, R 0.891, F1 0.851). Combinations with streak or value give only about +0.02.
The unrecorded value-head claim is only roughly true: value>7.6 instead of the time cutoff gives dev F1 0.818 (vs 0.84). value>7.5 & ep_trial<75 gives 0.841.
No future variables are used. prev_reward is observed and choice is the agent's own policy output, so no observed-only substitute is needed.
Rel position shows no artifact: precision is about 0.74 at every rel, including rel -3.
